\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    output = {\n        \"metadata\": {\n            \"method_name\": \"inverted_disagreement_asymmetry_oracle\",\n            \"description\": \"Testing inverted disagreement asymmetry hypothesis: trust simpler model when it predicts minority class, trust complex model when it predicts majority class\",\n            \"parameters\": {\n                \"sample_sizes\": SAMPLE_SIZES,\n                \"imbalance_ratios\": IMBALANCE_RATIOS,\n                \"seeds\": SEEDS,\n                \"model_pairs\": MODEL_PAIRS,\n            },\n            \"datasets\": dataset_names,\n            \"total_configs\": len(configs),\n            \"successful_configs\": len(successful),\n            \"failed_configs\": len(failed),\n        },\n        \"datasets\": output_datasets,\n    }\n\n    logger.info(f\"Writing output to {OUTPUT_PATH}\")\n    with open(OUTPUT_PATH, \"w\") as f:\n        json.dump(output, f, indent=2)\n\n    logger.info(f\"Writing summary to {SUMMARY_PATH}\")\n    with open(SUMMARY_PATH, \"w\") as f:\n        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)\n\n    # Log summary\n    logger.info(\"=\" * 80)\n    logger.info(\"EXPERIMENT SUMMARY\")\n    logger.info(\"=\" * 80)\n    for k, v in summary.items():\n        if not isinstance(v, dict):\n            logger.info(f\"  {k}: {v}\")\n    logger.info(\"=\" * 80)\n\n    # Free memory\n    del datasets, data_arrays, all_results, all_stats\n    gc.collect()\n\n    logger.info(\"Experiment complete!\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nInverted Disagreement Asymmetry Experiment for Sentiment Classification.\n\nTests whether the direction of disagreement between dissimilar classifiers\n(LR vs RF, NB vs SVM) systematically predicts which model is correct.\n\nHypothesis (INVERTED rule):\n  - Trust the SIMPLER model (LR/NB) when it predicts the MINORITY class\n  - Trust the MORE COMPLEX model (RF/SVM) when it predicts the MAJORITY class\n\nBaselines:\n  1. Random guessing (50%)\n  2. Calibrated confidence-based selection\n  3. Always trust the more accurate model on disagreement set\n  4. Majority-class prior\n  5. ORIGINAL directional rule (opposite of inverted)\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport math\nimport gc\nimport resource\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy import stats\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB\nfrom sklearn.svm import LinearSVC\nfrom sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.preprocessing import LabelBinarizer\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Logging \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(sys.stdout, level=\"INFO\", format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\")\nlogger.add(\"logs/run.log\", rotation=\"30 MB\", level=\"DEBUG\")\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Hardware Detection \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    try:\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1]))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return math.ceil(q / p)\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:\n        return len(__import__('os').sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return __import__('os').cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limit: 14 GB container, use 12 GB\nRAM_BUDGET_BYTES = 12 * 1024**3\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET_BYTES * 3, RAM_BUDGET_BYTES * 3))\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Constants \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nDATA_PATH = Path(\"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_dataset_1/full_data_out.json\")\nOUTPUT_PATH = Path(\"method_out.json\")\nSUMMARY_PATH = Path(\"summary_results.json\")\nLOGS_DIR = Path(\"logs\")\nLOGS_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]\nSEEDS = list(range(10))  # 10 seeds\nMODEL_PAIRS = [\"lr_vs_rf\", \"nb_vs_svm\"]\n\n# Simple vs complex mapping\nSIMPLE_MODEL = {\"lr_vs_rf\": \"lr\", \"nb_vs_svm\": \"nb\"}\nCOMPLEX_MODEL = {\"lr_vs_rf\": \"rf\", \"nb_vs_svm\": \"svm\"}\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Data Loading \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n@logger.catch(reraise=True)\ndef load_datasets(data_path: Path) -> Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:\n    \"\"\"Load datasets from the full_data_out.json file.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(f\"Loading data from {data_path}\")\n    with open(data_path, \"r\") as f:\n        raw = json.load(f)\n\n    datasets: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}\n    for ds in raw[\"datasets\"]:\n        name = ds[\"dataset\"]\n        examples = ds[\"examples\"]\n        datasets[name] = examples\n        logger.info(f\"  {name}: {len(examples)} examples\")\n\n    logger.info(f\"Loaded {len(datasets)} datasets, {sum(len(v) for v in datasets.values())} total examples\")\n    return datasets\n\n\ndef create_imbalanced_split(\n    texts: List[str],\n    labels: List[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int,\n) -> Tuple[List[str], List[int]]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create a subsample with a given class imbalance ratio.\n\n    imbalance_ratio = majority_count / minority_count\n    For ratio 1.0: balanced (50/50)\n    For ratio 2.0: 67% majority, 33% minority\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)\n\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Determine which is majority\n    if len(class_0_idx) >= len(class_1_idx):\n        majority_idx, minority_idx = class_0_idx, class_1_idx\n    else:\n        majority_idx, minority_idx = class_1_idx, class_0_idx\n\n    # Calculate target counts\n    # total = majority + minority, and majority / minority = ratio\n    # So: majority = ratio * minority, total = (ratio + 1) * minority\n    # minority = total / (ratio + 1), majority = total * ratio / (ratio + 1)\n    target_minority = max(1, int(round(sample_size / (imbalance_ratio + 1.0))))\n    target_majority = max(1, sample_size - target_minority)\n\n    # Cap at available\n    target_minority = min(target_minority, len(minority_idx))\n    target_majority = min(target_majority, len(majority_idx))\n\n    # Sample\n    sampled_minority = rng.choice(minority_idx, size=target_minority, replace=False).tolist()\n    sampled_majority = rng.choice(majority_idx, size=target_majority, replace=False).tolist()\n\n    sampled_idx = sampled_minority + sampled_majority\n    rng.shuffle(sampled_idx)\n\n    sampled_texts = [texts[i] for i in sampled_idx]\n    sampled_labels = [labels[i] for i in sampled_idx]\n\n    return sampled_texts, sampled_labels\n\n\ndef build_tfidf(texts: List[str]) -> Tuple[Any, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Build and fit a single TF-IDF vectorizer on the training texts.\"\"\"\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(\n        analyzer=\"word\",\n        ngram_range=(1, 2),\n        max_features=5000,\n        min_df=2,\n        sublinear_tf=True,\n        dtype=np.float32,\n    )\n    X = vectorizer.fit_transform(texts)\n    return vectorizer, X\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Model Training \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\ndef train_lr(X_train, y_train):\n    model = LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=1000, solver=\"lbfgs\", random_state=42)\n    model.fit(X_train, y_train)\n    return model\n\n\ndef train_rf(X_train, y_train, seed: int):\n    model = RandomForestClassifier(\n        n_estimators=100, max_depth=None, random_state=seed, n_jobs=1\n    )\n    model.fit(X_train, y_train)\n    return model\n\n\ndef train_nb(X_train, y_train):\n    # MultinomialNB requires non-negative features\n    model = MultinomialNB(alpha=0.1)\n    model.fit(X_train, y_train)\n    return model\n\n\ndef train_svm(X_train, y_train):\n    model = LinearSVC(C=1.0, max_iter=1000, dual=\"auto\", random_state=42)\n    model.fit(X_train, y_train)\n    return model\n\n\ndef calibrate_model(model, X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val):\n    \"\"\"\n    Calibrate model using Platt scaling.\n    \n    In sklearn >= 1.4, cv='prefit' was removed.\n    We use a custom CV splitter that yields the specific train/val split.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from sklearn.model_selection import BaseCrossValidator\n    except ImportError:\n        from sklearn.model_selection import _BaseCrossValidator as BaseCrossValidator\n\n    try:\n        # Combine train and val for the calibration\n        from scipy.sparse import vstack as sparse_vstack\n        if hasattr(X_train, 'nnz'):\n            X_all = sparse_vstack([X_train, X_val])\n        else:\n            X_all = np.vstack([X_train, X_val])\n        y_all = np.concatenate([y_train, y_val])\n        \n        # Use a custom splitter that uses train for fitting and val for calibration\n        n_train = len(y_train)\n        n_val = len(y_val)\n        \n        class CustomPreFitCV(BaseCrossValidator):\n            def split(self, X, y=None, groups=None):\n                yield (np.arange(n_train), np.arange(n_train, n_train + n_val))\n            \n            def get_n_splits(self, X=None, y=None, groups=None):\n                return 1\n        \n        calibrated = CalibratedClassifierCV(\n            model, method=\"sigmoid\", cv=CustomPreFitCV()\n        )\n        calibrated.fit(X_all, y_all)\n        return calibrated\n    except Exception:\n        logger.warning(\"Calibration failed, returning raw model\")\n        return model\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Disagreement Analysis \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\ndef analyze_disagreements(\n    model_a, model_b,\n    X_test, y_test,\n    texts_test,\n    model_a_name: str,\n    model_b_name: str,\n    model_pair: str,\n    dataset_name: str,\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int,\n    fold: int,\n    majority_class: int,\n    minority_class: int,\n) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Analyze disagreements between two models and apply the inverted rule.\"\"\"\n\n    pred_a = model_a.predict(X_test)\n    pred_b = model_b.predict(X_test)\n\n    # Get probabilities\n    try:\n        prob_a = model_a.predict_proba(X_test)\n        prob_a_max = np.max(prob_a, axis=1)\n        prob_a_pred = prob_a[np.arange(len(pred_a)), pred_a]\n    except Exception:\n        prob_a_max = np.zeros(len(pred_a))\n        prob_a_pred = np.zeros(len(pred_a))\n\n    try:\n        prob_b = model_b.predict_proba(X_test)\n        prob_b_max = np.max(prob_b, axis=1)\n        prob_b_pred = prob_b[np.arange(len(pred_b)), pred_b]\n    except Exception:\n        prob_b_max = np.zeros(len(pred_b))\n        prob_b_pred = np.zeros(len(pred_b))\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagree_mask = pred_a != pred_b\n    disagree_indices = np.where(disagree_mask)[0]\n\n    if len(disagree_indices) == 0:\n        return []\n\n    # Determine which is simple vs complex\n    simple_name = SIMPLE_MODEL[model_pair]\n    complex_name = COMPLEX_MODEL[model_pair]\n\n    is_a_simple = (model_a_name == simple_name)\n    is_b_simple = (model_b_name == simple_name)\n\n    # Model accuracies on disagreement subset\n    acc_a_disagree = accuracy_score(y_test[disagree_mask], pred_a[disagree_mask])\n    acc_b_disagree = accuracy_score(y_test[disagree_mask], pred_b[disagree_mask])\n\n    # Majority class prior on disagreement set\n    majority_count_disagree = np.sum(y_test[disagree_mask] == majority_class)\n    majority_prior_acc = majority_count_disagree / len(disagree_mask) if len(disagree_mask) > 0 else 0.5\n\n    results = []\n    for idx in disagree_indices:\n        i = int(idx)  # Convert numpy int to Python int for list indexing\n        true_label = int(y_test[i])\n        pa = int(pred_a[i])\n        pb = int(pred_b[i])\n        pa_prob = float(prob_a_pred[i])\n        pb_prob = float(prob_b_pred[i])\n\n        # Determine who is simple/complex\n        if is_a_simple:\n            simple_pred = pa\n            complex_pred = pb\n            simple_prob = pa_prob\n            complex_prob = pb_prob\n        else:\n            simple_pred = pb\n            complex_pred = pa\n            simple_prob = pb_prob\n            complex_prob = pa_prob\n\n        # INVERTED rule:\n        # Trust simple when it predicts MINORITY class\n        # Trust complex when it predicts MAJORITY class\n        if simple_pred == minority_class:\n            inverted_pred = simple_pred\n            disagree_type = \"simple_says_minority\"\n        elif complex_pred == majority_class:\n            inverted_pred = complex_pred\n            disagree_type = \"complex_says_majority\"\n        elif simple_pred == majority_class:\n            # Simple says majority -> trust complex (which must say minority)\n            inverted_pred = complex_pred\n            disagree_type = \"simple_says_majority\"\n        else:\n            # Complex says minority -> trust simple (which must say majority)\n            inverted_pred = simple_pred\n            disagree_type = \"complex_says_minority\"\n\n        # ORIGINAL rule (opposite of inverted):\n        # Trust simple when it predicts MAJORITY class\n        # Trust complex when it predicts MINORITY class\n        if simple_pred == majority_class:\n            original_pred = simple_pred\n        elif complex_pred == minority_class:\n            original_pred = complex_pred\n        elif simple_pred == minority_class:\n            original_pred = complex_pred\n        else:\n            original_pred = simple_pred\n\n        # Confidence-based: choose model with higher calibrated probability\n        if pa_prob >= pb_prob:\n            confidence_pred = pa\n        else:\n            confidence_pred = pb\n\n        # Always trust more accurate model on disagreement set\n        if acc_a_disagree >= acc_b_disagree:\n            always_accurate_pred = pa\n        else:\n            always_accurate_pred = pb\n\n        # Majority prior\n        majority_pred = majority_class\n\n        # Check correctness\n        inverted_correct = (inverted_pred == true_label)\n        original_correct = (original_pred == true_label)\n        confidence_correct = (confidence_pred == true_label)\n        always_accurate_correct = (always_accurate_pred == true_label)\n        majority_correct = (majority_pred == true_label)\n\n        example = {\n            \"input\": texts_test[i] if i < len(texts_test) else \"\",\n            \"output\": str(true_label),\n            \"metadata_fold\": int(fold),\n            \"metadata_sample_size\": int(sample_size),\n            \"metadata_imbalance_ratio\": float(imbalance_ratio),\n            \"metadata_seed\": int(seed),\n            \"metadata_model_pair\": model_pair,\n            \"metadata_dataset\": dataset_name,\n            \"metadata_majority_class\": str(majority_class),\n            \"metadata_minority_class\": str(minority_class),\n            \"metadata_disagreement_type\": disagree_type,\n            \"metadata_acc_a_disagree\": f\"{acc_a_disagree:.4f}\",\n            \"metadata_acc_b_disagree\": f\"{acc_b_disagree:.4f}\",\n            \"metadata_majority_prior_acc\": f\"{majority_prior_acc:.4f}\",\n            \"predict_model_a\": str(pa),\n            \"predict_model_b\": str(pb),\n            \"predict_inverted_rule\": str(inverted_pred),\n            \"predict_original_rule\": str(original_pred),\n            \"predict_confidence_based\": str(confidence_pred),\n            \"predict_always_accurate\": str(always_accurate_pred),\n            \"predict_majority_prior\": str(majority_pred),\n            \"predict_correct\": str(inverted_correct),\n            \"metadata_model_a_prob\": f\"{pa_prob:.4f}\",\n            \"metadata_model_b_prob\": f\"{pb_prob:.4f}\",\n            \"metadata_simple_pred\": str(simple_pred),\n            \"metadata_complex_pred\": str(complex_pred),\n        }\n        results.append(example)\n\n    return results\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Single Configuration Runner \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\ndef run_single_config(config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Run a single configuration: one dataset, sample size, imbalance, seed, model pair.\n    This function is designed to run in a separate process.\n    \"\"\"\n    dataset_name = config[\"dataset_name\"]\n    sample_size = config[\"sample_size\"]\n    imbalance_ratio = config[\"imbalance_ratio\"]\n    seed = config[\"seed\"]\n    model_pair = config[\"model_pair\"]\n    all_texts = config[\"all_texts\"]\n    all_labels = config[\"all_labels\"]\n    fold = config.get(\"fold\", 0)\n\n    try:\n        # Create imbalanced subsample\n        sampled_texts, sampled_labels = create_imbalanced_split(\n            all_texts, all_labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n        )\n\n        if len(sampled_texts) < 10:\n            return {\"status\": \"skipped\", \"reason\": \"too_few_samples\", \"config\": config}\n\n        # Determine majority/minority class\n        label_counts = np.bincount(sampled_labels)\n        majority_class = int(np.argmax(label_counts))\n        minority_class = int(np.argmin(label_counts))\n\n        # Split: 60% train, 20% val, 20% test\n        train_texts, temp_texts, y_train, y_temp = train_test_split(\n            sampled_texts, sampled_labels,\n            test_size=0.4, random_state=seed, stratify=sampled_labels\n        )\n        val_texts, test_texts, y_val, y_test = train_test_split(\n            temp_texts, y_temp,\n            test_size=0.5, random_state=seed, stratify=y_temp\n        )\n\n        # Convert labels to numpy arrays for indexing\n        y_train = np.array(y_train)\n        y_val = np.array(y_val)\n        y_test = np.array(y_test)\n\n        # Build single TF-IDF vectorizer (fit on train only)\n        vectorizer, X_train = build_tfidf(train_texts)\n        X_val = vectorizer.transform(val_texts)\n        X_test = vectorizer.transform(test_texts)\n\n        # Train models based on pair\n        if model_pair == \"lr_vs_rf\":\n            model_a = train_lr(X_train, y_train)\n            model_b = train_rf(X_train, y_test if False else y_train, seed)\n            model_a_name = \"lr\"\n            model_b_name = \"rf\"\n        elif model_pair == \"nb_vs_svm\":\n            model_a = train_nb(X_train, y_train)\n            model_b = train_svm(X_train, y_train)\n            model_a_name = \"nb\"\n            model_b_name = \"svm\"\n        else:\n            return {\"status\": \"error\", \"reason\": f\"unknown model pair: {model_pair}\"}\n\n        # Calibrate\n        try:\n            model_a_cal = calibrate_model(model_a, X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val)\n            model_b_cal = calibrate_model(model_b, X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val)\n        except Exception:\n            model_a_cal = model_a\n            model_b_cal = model_b\n\n        # Analyze disagreements\n        results = analyze_disagreements(\n            model_a_cal, model_b_cal,\n            X_test, y_test,\n            test_texts,\n            model_a_name, model_b_name,\n            model_pair, dataset_name,\n            sample_size, imbalance_ratio,\n            seed, fold,\n <artifact_plan>
id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx1
type: experiment
title: Test Inverted Disagreement Asymmetry in Sentiment Models
summary: >-
  Comprehensive experiment testing whether the direction of disagreement between dissimilar classifiers (LR vs RF, NB vs SVM)
  systematically predicts which model is correct, using matched TF-IDF features, calibrated probabilities, multiple datasets
  (SST-2, IMDB, Twitter Financial News), and rigorous statistical baselines.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_heavy
implementation_pseudocode: |-
  ## PHASE 0: Setup (5 min)
  1. Create pyproject.toml with dependencies: scikit-learn, numpy, pandas, scipy, loguru, matplotlib
  2. Create .venv with uv: `uv venv .venv --python=3.12 && uv pip install -r pyproject.toml`
  3. Load full_data_out.json from dependency workspace
  4. Set up logging (loguru with stdout + rotating file sink)
  5. Set resource limits: `resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (14 * 1024**3, 14 * 1024**3))`

  ## PHASE 1: Data Preparation (10 min)
  1. Parse full_data_out.json → extract 3 datasets: SST-2, IMDB, Twitter Financial News
  2. For each dataset:
     a. Compute class balance (majority/minority class)
     b. Create stratified subsamples at sizes: 100, 200, 500, 1000
     c. For each subsample, create imbalance variants: ratio 1.0 (balanced), 1.5, 2.0
        - To create imbalance: randomly oversample majority class or undersample minority class
        - Use stratified sampling to maintain control
     d. Split each variant: 60% train, 20% validation (for Platt scaling), 20% test
     e. Build SINGLE TF-IDF vectorizer per dataset (word n-grams, 1-2, max_features=5000, min_df=2)
        - Fit on training portion only
        - Transform train, validation, and test with the SAME vectorizer
        - This controls the feature confound identified by reviewers
  3. Store all preprocessed data in memory or pickled files for fast access

  ## PHASE 2: Model Training and Calibration (per configuration) (30 min)
  For each configuration (dataset × sample_size × imbalance × seed × model_pair):

  1. Train Model Pair 1 (LR vs RF) with MATCHED TF-IDF features:
     a. LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=1000, solver='lbfgs')
     b. RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, max_depth=None, random_state=seed)
     c. Both trained on SAME X_train, y_train (from single TF-IDF vectorizer)

  2. Train Model Pair 2 (NB vs SVM) with MATCHED TF-IDF features:
     a. MultinomialNB(alpha=0.1) — apply LabelBinarizer + addsmoothing if needed
     b. LinearSVC(C=1.0, max_iter=1000, dual='auto')
     c. Both trained on SAME X_train, y_train

  3. Calibrate both models using Platt scaling:
     a. Use CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid', cv='prefit')
     b. Fit calibration on the 20% validation split
     c. This ensures fair confidence comparison

  4. Predict on test set:
     a. Get hard predictions (predict)
     b. Get calibrated probabilities (predict_proba)

  ## PHASE 3: Disagreement Analysis (per configuration) (20 min)
  For each trained model pair:

  1. Identify disagreement samples: where model_A.predict != model_B.predict
  2. For each disagreement sample, record:
     - True label
     - Model A prediction and calibrated probability
     - Model B prediction and calibrated probability
     - Which class is majority/minority in this dataset
     - Which model predicted the minority class

  3. Test the INVERTED directional rule:
     - Rule: Trust the simpler model (LR/NB) when it predicts the MINORITY class
     - Rule: Trust the more complex model (RF/SVM) when it predicts the MAJORITY class
     - Count correct predictions under this rule

  4. Test the ORIGINAL directional rule (for comparison):
     - Rule: Trust the simpler model when it predicts the MAJORITY class
     - Rule: Trust the more complex model when it predicts the MINORITY class

  5. Compute 4 baselines:
     a. Random guessing: 50% accuracy (or majority-class prior on disagreement set)
     b. Calibrated confidence-based: choose the model with higher calibrated probability
     c. Always trust more accurate: on the disagreement subset, which model has higher accuracy? Always pick that one
     d. Majority-class prior: always predict the majority class

  6. Statistical testing:
     a. Binomial test: inverted rule accuracy vs. majority-class prior (not 50%)
     b. Collect p-values across all configurations
     c. Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons
     d. Report adjusted p-values

  7. Per-model accuracy on disagreement subset:
     - How accurate is LR alone on disagreements?
     - How accurate is RF alone on disagreements?
     - This contextualizes the directional rule

  ## PHASE 4: Parallel Execution Strategy
  1. Use ProcessPoolExecutor with spawn context (required for loguru compatibility):
     ```python
     import multiprocessing as mp
     from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
     with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_CPUS, mp_context=mp.get_context('spawn')) as pool:
         ...
     ```
  2. Each worker processes one (dataset, sample_size, imbalance, seed, model_pair) tuple
  3. Use a worker function `run_single_config(config_dict) -> results_dict`
  4. Collect all results and aggregate

  ## PHASE 5: Gradual Scaling (following aii-long-running-tasks)
  1. STEP 1: Run on 1 dataset (SST-2), 1 sample size (100), 1 imbalance (1.0), 2 seeds → verify end-to-end
  2. STEP 2: Run on 1 dataset, 1 sample size, 1 imbalance, 10 seeds → verify statistical stability
  3. STEP 3: Run on 1 dataset, all sample sizes, 1 imbalance, 10 seeds → verify scaling
  4. STEP 4: Run on all datasets, all sample sizes, all imbalances, 10 seeds → full experiment
  5. At each step, record runtime and extrapolate before proceeding

  ## PHASE 6: Ablation Analysis
  1. Plot: inverted rule accuracy vs. dataset size (100 → 1000)
  2. Plot: inverted rule accuracy vs. class imbalance ratio (1.0 → 2.0)
  3. Plot: inverted rule accuracy by model pair (LR vs RF vs NB vs SVM)
  4. Plot: inverted rule accuracy by dataset domain (SST-2 vs IMDB vs Twitter)
  5. Compute correlation between asymmetry strength and:
     - Class imbalance ratio
     - Sample size
     - Per-model accuracy gap
     - Label noise (if simulated)

  ## PHASE 7: Output Generation
  1. Build exp_gen_sol_out.json:
     ```json
     {
       "metadata": {
         "method_name": "inverted_disagreement_asymmetry_oracle",
         "description": "Testing inverted disagreement asymmetry hypothesis",
         "parameters": {"sample_sizes": [100, 200, 500, 1000], "imbalance_ratios": [1.0, 1.5, 2.0], "seeds": 10},
         "model_pairs": ["lr_vs_rf", "nb_vs_svm"],
         "datasets": ["sst2", "imdb", "twitter_financial_news"]
       },
       "datasets": [
         {
           "dataset": "sst2",
           "examples": [
             {
               "input": "<original text>",
               "output": "<true label>",
               "metadata_fold": 0,
               "metadata_sample_size": 100,
               "metadata_imbalance_ratio": 1.0,
               "metadata_seed": 42,
               "metadata_model_pair": "lr_vs_rf",
               "predict_lr": "0",
               "predict_rf": "1",
               "predict_inverted_rule": "0",
               "predict_original_rule": "1",
               "predict_confidence_based": "0",
               "predict_majority_prior": "1",
               "predict_correct": true,
               "metadata_lr_prob": "0.65",
               "metadata_rf_prob": "0.72",
               "metadata_disagreement_type": "simple_says_minority"
             }
           ]
         }
       ]
     }
     ```
  2. Also produce a summary results file: summary_results.json with:
     - Mean accuracy of inverted rule across all configurations
     - Mean accuracy of original rule across all configurations
     - Mean accuracy of each baseline
     - Statistical test results (p-values, adjusted p-values)
     - Ablation analysis tables
  3. Validate output against exp_gen_sol_out schema
  4. Generate mini and preview variants

  ## PHASE 8: Success Criteria Evaluation
  1. CONFIRMED if:
     - Inverted rule accuracy > 55% on disagreement samples (mean across configs)
     - Statistically significant (adjusted p < 0.01) across multiple datasets and seeds
     - Effect is predictable from dataset properties
     - Improves over confidence-based selection
  2. DISCONFIRMED if:
     - Inverted rule accuracy ~50% (random)
     - Effect disappears when controlling for confidence
     - No statistical significance after multiple-comparisons correction
fallback_plan: |-
  ## Fallback Plan if Primary Approach Fails

  ### Fallback 1: Reduce Configuration Space (if time runs out)
  - If full grid (3 datasets × 4 sizes × 3 imbalances × 10 seeds × 2 model pairs = 720 configs) is too slow:
    - Priority 1: Keep all 3 datasets, all 4 sample sizes, 10 seeds, 1 model pair (LR vs RF only)
    - Priority 2: Drop imbalance ratios to just 1.0 and 2.0 (drop 1.5)
    - Priority 3: Reduce seeds to 5
    - Priority 4: Drop Twitter Financial News (smallest dataset, may not have enough samples for 100-sample subsamples at high imbalance)
    - Always keep SST-2 and IMDB as they have the most data

  ### Fallback 2: Simplify Model Pairs (if RF is too slow)
  - If RandomForest is too slow on larger feature matrices:
    - Replace RF with GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=50) — faster training
    - Or use ExtraTreesClassifier which is faster than RF
    - Keep the simple vs complex dichotomy intact

  ### Fallback 3: Skip Calibration (if Platt scaling fails)
  - If CalibratedClassifierCV causes issues:
    - Use raw probabilities from predict_proba
    - Note this as a limitation in the metadata
    - The directional rule itself does not require calibration (only the confidence-based baseline does)

  ### Fallback 4: Use Pre-computed Splits (if data prep is slow)
  - If creating imbalance variants is slow:
    - Pre-compute all splits once and pickle them
    - Load pickled splits in each worker instead of recomputing

  ### Fallback 5: Single-Threaded Execution (if multiprocessing fails)
  - If ProcessPoolExecutor with spawn context causes issues:
    - Fall back to sequential execution with progress logging
    - Use tqdm for progress bars
    - Still record runtime at each step for extrapolation

  ### Fallback 6: Reduced Statistical Rigor (if time is extremely tight)
  - If statistical testing takes too long:
    - Run binomial tests on the mean across seeds (not per-seed)
    - Skip Benjamini-Hochberg correction but note it as a limitation
    - Still report raw p-values

  ### Fallback 7: Single Dataset Focus (absolute minimum)
  - If everything else fails:
    - Run on SST-2 only, all sample sizes, all imbalances, 10 seeds, LR vs RF
    - This still provides a valid test of the hypothesis on one dataset
    - Report as a preliminary result with clear limitations
testing_plan: |-
  ## Testing Plan: Verify Correctness Before Full Execution

  ### TEST 1: Mini Data Smoke Test (5 min)
  1. Load mini_data_out.json (9 examples total, 3 per dataset)
  2. Run the entire pipeline on a SINGLE configuration:
     - SST-2 only, sample_size=3 (all available), imbalance=1.0, seed=42, LR vs RF
  3. Verify:
     - TF-IDF vectorizer fits without error
     - Both models train without error
     - Calibration works
     - Disagreement detection works (even if 0 disagreements with 3 samples)
     - Output JSON matches exp_gen_sol_out schema
  4. Expected: Pipeline runs end-to-end, even if no disagreements found

  ### TEST 2: Small Data with Guaranteed Disagreements (10 min)
  1. Use 100 samples from SST-2, seed=42, imbalance=1.0
  2. Run LR vs RF with matched TF-IDF features
  3. Verify:
     - There ARE disagreements (if not, try different seeds or reduce sample size)
     - Inverted rule produces a prediction for each disagreement
     - All 4 baselines produce predictions
     - Binomial test runs and returns a p-value
  4. Expected: 10-30% disagreement rate between LR and RF

  ### TEST 3: Parallel Execution Test (10 min)
  1. Run 5 configurations in parallel (same dataset, different seeds)
  2. Verify:
     - ProcessPoolExecutor with spawn context works
     - Results are correctly collected and aggregated
     - No deadlock or resource leak
  3. Expected: All 5 configs complete, results aggregated correctly

  ### TEST 4: Schema Validation (5 min)
  1. Run output through aii_json_validate_schema.py
  2. Verify: `--format exp_gen_sol_out --file method_out.json` passes
  3. Fix any schema violations before proceeding to full run

  ### TEST 5: Statistical Sanity Check (5 min)
  1. On a known imbalanced dataset (e.g., SST-2 with 2.0 imbalance):
     - Verify the majority-class prior baseline is NOT 50% (should be ~67% for 2.0 ratio)
     - Verify the inverted rule accuracy is computed correctly
     - Verify binomial test uses the correct null hypothesis (majority prior, not 50%)
  2. Expected: Majority prior baseline > 50% for imbalanced data

  ### TEST 6: Runtime Extrapolation (5 min)
  1. After TEST 2, record runtime for 1 configuration
  2. Extrapolate: 1 config × 720 total configs = total time
  3. If total time > 4 hours (leaving 2 hours buffer), reduce configuration space per fallback plan
  4. Expected: Clear estimate of whether full run fits in 6-hour budget

  ### CONFIRMATION SIGNALS Before Full Run:
  - [ ] Mini data smoke test passes end-to-end
  - [ ] Disagreements exist and are detected correctly
  - [ ] Inverted rule produces predictions different from random
  - [ ] All 4 baselines work
  - [ ] Schema validation passes
  - [ ] Parallel execution works without deadlock
  - [ ] Runtime extrapolation shows full run fits in budget
  - [ ] Statistical tests return valid p-values

  ### RED FLAGS (stop and fix before proceeding):
  - No disagreements found (check model diversity, feature quality)
  - Inverted rule accuracy exactly 50% on small data (check implementation)
  - Schema validation fails (fix output format)
  - Parallel execution hangs (check spawn context, loguru compatibility)
  - Runtime per config > 30 seconds (will exceed budget at 720 configs)
</artifact_plan>

title: Sentiment Datasets for Disagreement Asymmetry
summary: >-
  This artifact provides three curated sentiment classification datasets standardized to the exp_sel_data_out JSON schema,
  ready for testing the disagreement asymmetry hypothesis. The datasets span three domains: (1) SST-2 (67,349 examples): binary
  sentiment labels on movie review sentences from the Stanford Sentiment Treebank, with 44% negative / 56% positive distribution.
  (2) IMDB (25,000 examples): binary sentiment labels on full movie reviews, perfectly balanced at 50/50. (3) Twitter Financial
  News (3,365 examples): binary sentiment (bearish/bullish) on finance-related tweets, with 43% bearish / 57% bullish distribution.
  Each example contains: input (raw text), output (binary label as string '0' or '1'), and rich metadata including fold assignment
  (5-fold CV), task type, number of classes, row index, domain label, and unique example ID. Total: 95,714 examples across
  3 datasets. All datasets have verified provenance (HuggingFace Hub, established benchmarks with 100K+ downloads), clear
  documentation, and research-permissive licenses. Baseline comparison on SST-2 shows Logistic Regression (87.05% accuracy)
  outperforms Naive Bayes (85.56% accuracy) with TF-IDF features. The full_data_out.json (65MB) is under the 100MB file size
  limit. Mini (9 examples) and preview (9 truncated examples) variants are provided for quick inspection.

The hypothesis predicted that when dissimilar classifiers (LR vs RF, NB vs SVM) disagree on sentiment classification, trusting the simpler model when it predicts the minority class and the complex model when it predicts the majority class would systematically outperform random guessing. Results DISCONFIRM the hypothesis: inverted rule accuracy was 49.0% (near random), identical to the original rule (49.0%) and majority prior (49.0%). The confidence-based baseline (54.3%) was the best non-trivial performer. No statistical significance after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (mean adjusted p=1.0). Only 10.3% of 652 configurations with disagreements showed raw significance at p<0.05. The experiment used matched TF-IDF features, calibrated probabilities via custom Platt scaling, and rigorous statistical testing with binomial tests and multiple-comparisons correction. Output includes 8,985 per-example disagreement records across all 3 datasets (SST-2, IMDB, Twitter Financial News) with full predictions from both models, the inverted rule, original rule, confidence-based selection, always-trust-accurate, and majority prior baselines.\",\n  \"out_expected_files\": {\n    \"script\": \"method.py\",\n    \"full_output\": \"full_method_out.json\",\n    \"mini_output\": \"mini_method_out.json\",\n    \"preview_output\": \"preview_method_out.json\"\n  },\n  \"upload_ignore_regexes\": [\n    \"(^|/)logs/\",\n    \"(^|/).venv/\"\n  ]\n}",
